Staff Frontend Engineer

An overview of this role

As a Staff Frontend Engineer on the Core DevOps team, you'll provide technical leadership across your team and adjacent teams. You'll solve complex frontend problems, deliver large features with minimal guidance, and improve the architecture and standards that help teams move faster without compromising quality.

You'll work with product, design, engineering managers, and engineers across product groups to shape product experiences and frontend architecture for a global platform. This includes how teams use agentic artificial intelligence in engineering workflows and user experiences.

At GitLab, we build an all-remote, artificial intelligence-powered DevSecOps platform. You'll help shape product experiences and frontend architecture that enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the technical design and delivery of large, complex frontend initiatives across multiple teams.
  • Drive frontend platform, design system, and shared architecture strategy for long-term scalability.
  • Define and improve standards for versioning, testing, documentation, accessibility, security, performance, and maintainability.
  • Lead modernization of a monolith or legacy frontend architecture toward modular, reusable, and independently deployable systems.
  • Establish versioned module or host contracts and build, test, deploy, release, and rollback practices for safe operations.
  • Create shared patterns for dependency management, design system integration, observability, error isolation, and performance budgets.
  • Guide technical direction through clear written proposals and architectural leadership. Partner with product and engineering leaders on platform roadmaps, technical debt, and investment trade-offs.
  • Mentor senior and intermediate engineers. Establish guardrails for artificial-intelligence-assisted and agentic workflows that protect code quality, security, privacy, and evaluation standards.

What you’ll bring

  • A sustained record of technical leadership across teams or a broad product area.
  • Deep frontend architecture and production experience in complex web applications.
  • Experience scaling or governing a design system, frontend platform, or shared component architecture.
  • Experience with modular frontend architecture in production, such as package encapsulation, Web Components, frontend islands, runtime composition, or an equivalent architecture.
  • Experience creating alignment without formal authority through clear written proposals and decision records.
  • Experience balancing user outcomes, delivery speed, technical health, and long-term platform investment.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and shaping standards through code review and documentation, including evaluating and improving artificial-intelligence-assisted or agentic engineering workflows.
  • Helpful, but not required: experience with Vue, React, Angular, TypeScript, or JavaScript; PostgreSQL, Redis, or object storage; representational state transfer or GraphQL application programming interfaces; Kubernetes, Google Kubernetes Engine, Docker, or Google Cloud Platform; and observability tools such as Prometheus or Sentry.

About the team

On the Core DevOps team, we own core repository capabilities, from Git command-line operations to web-based code exploration. We develop new features and platforms, improve existing capabilities, and improve maintainability, accessibility, performance, and workflows for teams using artificial-intelligence-assisted development tools.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Flexible Paid Time Off

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Metronome is a usage-based billing platform and a Stripe product. It helps modern software companies launch products faster, offer flexible pricing models, and streamline finance workflows.

The Metronome Integration Engineering team sits at the intersection of sales, growth, product, and research and development. We own the technical aspects of the customer lifecycle after a sale and before the customer transitions to our post-implementation teams.

What you'll do

As an Integration Engineer, you’ll help customers implement Metronome successfully and realize value quickly. You’ll lead technical work across requirements gathering, solution and integration design, configuration, testing, data migration, launch, and handoff.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct discovery and scoping to understand customers’ challenges across billing, product launches, pricing and packaging, quote-to-cash, customer experience, and related areas.
  • Support customers throughout the implementation lifecycle, including requirements gathering, technical design, integration design, testing, data migration, and launch.
  • Provide expert guidance on usage-based pricing and consumption-based business models.
  • Configure Metronome’s platform on behalf of customers.
  • Design integrations between Metronome’s APIs and customers’ business systems—including CRM and CPQ platforms, payment and tax systems, ERP and billing providers, and reporting and analytics tools—in alignment with Metronome best practices.
  • Serve as a liaison between customers and Metronome’s research and development teams, advocating for customer needs and feature requests.
  • Partner with implementation managers and other project-team members to provide visibility into progress and proactively identify risks and issues.
  • Build relationships across customer organizations, from day-to-day operators to C-suite executives. Meet customers in person when doing so will improve the engagement.
  • Advise customers on integrating Metronome into their systems and help shape their pricing and packaging strategies.
  • Ensure an effective handoff to Customer Success and Technical Support.

You’ll work with some of Metronome’s most strategic customers. These engagements will be complex, deep, and highly technical. Metronome directly influences how modern software companies monetize their products, and this team is on the front lines of that work.

Metronome operates with a startup mindset within Stripe. There is a significant opportunity for people with initiative to influence our direction, build processes from zero to one, and make a meaningful impact.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements below. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are helpful but not required.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in technical or customer-facing roles involving SaaS products, such as sales engineering, solutions architecture, technical account management, or deployment strategy.
  • Experience leading complex implementations for enterprise technology companies.
  • Experience working in fast-moving environments that value initiative and ownership.
  • Ability to quickly learn and communicate technical concepts to technical, go-to-market, and finance stakeholders.
  • Interest in building and improving go-to-market playbooks, processes, and reusable assets.
  • Ability to travel approximately 30% of the time, depending on customer needs.

Preferred qualifications

  • Deep knowledge of quote-to-cash processes, including experience integrating with or working alongside platforms such as Salesforce, NetSuite, CPQ systems, and the Stripe ecosystem.
  • Experience as a software engineer, product manager, or in another technical role.
  • Strong understanding of project- and program-management fundamentals.
  • Experience working with stakeholders in finance, engineering, product, sales operations, or billing operations.
  • Experience with logs, metrics, billing, finance, infrastructure, or financial tooling and concepts.

Headquarters: Vancouver
 
URL: https://www.roveconcepts.com/

Company: Rove Next, by Rove Concepts
Location: Remote. Open across the Americas and Europe.
Hours: Full-time overlap with Pacific or Eastern time. This is a requirement, not a preference.
Type: Independent contractor, full time

About the role

Rove Next is a new premium line from Rove Concepts, a Vancouver-based modern furniture brand selling direct to consumer across Canada and the US. Rove Next launches with improved versions of our best-selling pieces, and it needs its own marketing built from the ground up.

That's this role. You'll own how Rove Next reaches customers and keeps them, starting with email and lifecycle. The goal is a marketing function that scales through AI and systems rather than through headcount, and the advantage here is that you're building it clean rather than inheriting one.

This is not a coordination role. We need someone who takes a problem and builds the answer, and who catches things before they reach leadership.

Scope

Initially focused on Rove Next, with room to expand across the Rove Concepts group as the brand grows.

What you'll own

Email and lifecycle as our primary owned channel. Campaign calendar, flows, segmentation, deliverability, list health. We run on Klaviyo.

Quality control on everything that ships. Copy, creative, link destinations, offers, regional versions. If something goes out wrong, it was yours to catch.

Building AI into the daily work. Not proposing it, shipping it.

Working alongside our lifecycle and email team, our designers, and our external ads partner to keep the calendar moving.

Translating results into plain business language. What we spent, what we made, what we'd do differently.

Must-haves

Five or more years in ecommerce or DTC marketing with real ownership of email and lifecycle. Klaviyo or a comparable ESP.

Evidence that you build with AI yourself rather than assigning it. When you hit a wall, your instinct should be to build through it, not to raise a ticket and wait.

Fluent, native-level English, written and spoken. This one is non-negotiable. You will be writing copy that goes out to our customers under our name, so we need someone who can hear the difference between a line that sounds premium and one that sounds like a discount retailer.

A strong eye. You can look at an asset and tell whether the destination matches the promise, whether the tone is right, and whether the offer math actually adds up.

Comfortable being told when something isn't landing, and comfortable telling us the same.

Nice to have

Furniture, home, or another considered-purchase category with a long buying cycle. Shopify, GA4 and Meta Ads familiarity. Experience holding a team to brand guidelines.

What success looks like

Flow revenue grows as a share of total email revenue. Work stops reaching leadership with errors in it. AI is doing measurable work inside the function within 90 days, rather than sitting in a proposal.

Compensation

$3,500 to $4,500 USD per month depending on experience. Independent contractor.

How to apply

Send your CV and in a few lines, tell us two things:

One AI workflow or automation you built yourself in a real business. What it did, and what it saved.

One time you caught something before it shipped that nobody else had noticed.

Please also include a short voice note, around 60 seconds, introducing yourself and telling us what you'd want to know before writing your first email for us.

Shortlisted candidates will be asked to complete a short paid project.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/rove-concepts-marketing-manager-ai-and-lifecycle

Headquarters: United States
 
URL: https://icarusdigitalmarketing.com/

Performance Creative Strategist and AI Producer

Remote | Full time | Paid 30-day working trial

Icarus Digital Marketing builds and scales direct-response ecommerce brands, including brands in difficult and restricted categories. We are hiring a hands-on performance creative operator to work directly with the owners on our internal portfolio of brands.

This is not a conventional graphic-design role. We need someone who understands why Meta ads convert and can personally turn that understanding into high-quality static and video creative using current AI production tools.

You may come from dropshipping, affiliate marketing, DTC, a performance agency, or a creative media-buying background. We care more about commercial judgment, production ability, speed, and proof of work than polished credentials.

The work

You will use and help improve our internal Creative Cockpit. It takes a brand from research and foundational strategy through campaign creation, production, review, and delivery. For each brand, the system holds brand assets and voice, customer language and audience psychology, pains and desires, necessary beliefs, competitor intelligence, awareness levels, angles, hooks, offer context, prior creative, winners, and performance signals.

Your job is to turn that intelligence into creative that can sell.

• Read campaign briefs, audience research, voice-of-customer material, and brand strategy documents.

• Decide what each batch should test and why.

• Source and analyse strong visual and structural references.

• Develop angles, hooks, scripts, concepts, storyboards, and landing-page direction.

• Personally produce static ads and short-form video ads.

• Use AI image, video, voice, and editing tools at a high level.

• Create meaningful variants without producing repetitive AI slop.

• Review work for persuasion, visual quality, brand fit, platform fit, and compliance.

• Refine weak generations rather than accepting the first output.

• Package approved assets for launch and document what each concept tests.

• Read results and use the learning to plan the next batch.

What you must be good at

• Direct-response advertising and Meta creative strategy

• Audience psychology and voice-of-customer interpretation

• Awareness levels, hooks, angles, mechanisms, objections, offers, and message-market fit

• Understanding when an ad should lead to a PDP, advertorial, listicle, quiz, or sales page

• Static ad, UGC, and short-form video production

• Visual-reference analysis and controlled recreation

• Current AI image and video workflows using tools such as Seedance, Google Flow/Omni, Nano Banana/Gemini, GPT Image, Higgsfield, Kling, Sora, Veo, or comparable tools

• Editing, compositing, pacing, captions, sound, and final polish

• Fast, organised batch production

• Reading creative performance and choosing the next test

You are probably not right for this role if

• Your portfolio is mostly branding, organic social content, or attractive design without performance context.

• You call every asset “scroll-stopping” but cannot explain the audience belief or conversion mechanism.

• You are a strategist who depends on other people to make the work.

• You are a tool operator who needs someone else to provide every hook, angle, script, and decision.

• You use one prompt, accept the first output, and call it AI production.

• You cannot show exactly what you personally contributed to portfolio examples.

• You dislike volume, iteration, testing, or direct feedback.

What success looks like

Within 30 days, you can understand our strategy packs and operating system, take a structured brief from research to finished assets with limited supervision, produce a useful weekly mix of static and video concepts, explain the reason for every important decision, maintain quality while moving quickly, and suggest practical improvements to the workflow.

Compensation

The role begins with a fully paid 30-day working trial at USD $2,000. If the fit is strong, it becomes a long-term full-time position expected to pay USD $2,000 to $3,000 per month, based on demonstrated level, with additional performance upside available for an exceptional long-term operator.

We care about ability, English comprehension, reliability, some overlap with our working hours, and quality of output.

How to apply

Do not send a generic cover letter. Message Simon on WhatsApp at +353 86 349 5073 and begin with: I make the work.

• Send three Meta ads you personally made or materially directed.

• For each example, state exactly what you did and explain the audience, angle, hook, and intended next step in the funnel.

• Share any useful performance context you are permitted to disclose. Redacted evidence is acceptable.

• Show one weak or failed creative and explain what you learned or changed.

• List the AI tools you use in real production and explain your normal workflow from reference to finished asset.

• Send a Loom of no more than five minutes. Choose one Meta ad you respect, explain why it works, and describe the next three variants you would test.

• State your location, timezone, availability, and expected monthly compensation after the trial.

Applications without the requested evidence will not be reviewed. Shortlisted candidates will complete a small paid practical exercise before the 30-day trial.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/icarus-digital-marketing-performance-creative-strategist-and-ai-producer
